newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin cuts maturity for Jan 28 bond sale. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin cuts maturity for Jan 28 bond sale. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry will auction an unspecified tranche of one-year bonds, instead of originally planned four-year bond auction, on January 28, the ministry said on Friday.

"We have changed the maturity to suit the ministry's needs, and the auction will show whether the current interbank market situation is favourable for one-year bonds," Juraj Macejka, head of the ministry's State Final Account Department, told Reuters.

The first issue of bonds this year, which will carry a 10.0 percent coupon paid semi-annually, will have no limit price set on bids (corrects conditions of bids from "will have a minimum price set at par"). The bonds will hold a nominal value of 100,000 crowns, the central bank said in a statement.
In the last auction of similar bonds on October 15, in which 2.179 billion crowns of bids were accepted from the total demand of 4.58 billion, the coupon was set at 9.0 percent.

Slovak interbank money market rates fell to a range of between 20.8 and 25.8 percent in early activity on Friday, with rates fluctuating at all maturities amid a liquidity crunch this week. Interbank rates hit record highs of 27.3 percent on Wednesday. Over a week ago rates ranged around 15-17 percent.
Earlier this month, the ministry published its bond and T-bill issue schedule for the first quarter, according to which it is planning to issue two four-year bonds, and one five-year bond.
Macejka declined to say wheather the ministry was considering any further changes to the original plan.
The Slovakia's overall 1997 state budget deficit is planned at 36.9 billion crowns, compared with a deficit of 27 billion crowns last year.
The government plans issuing 70 billion crowns worth of its securities on domestic markets this year.
